title: Pesticides and their effects
notes: [Remember] Pesticides are chemicals that kill pests: insecticides (insects), herbicides (weeds), fungicides (fungi), rodenticides (rats) — e.g. DDT, BHC, malathion, 2,4-D.
[Remember] Effects on pests: target kill and crop protection; effects beyond target — killing of pollinators and predators, pest resurgence and resistance after repeated use.
[Understand] Human-health effects: acute poisoning (nausea, tremor) and chronic effects (organ damage, suspected carcinogenicity); Terai farm workers face the highest exposure risk.

[Understand] Environmental effects: soil-microbe loss and fertility fall; water pollution and fish kills; biomagnification up food chains (classic case: DDT in birds); harm to bees and natural enemies.
[Apply] Safe-use table — read label dose, wear protection, spray with wind direction, observe waiting period before harvest, never wash sprayers in ponds or rivers.
[Analyze] Chemical control vs biological control vs IPM (Integrated Pest Management: resistant varieties + predators + need-based minimal spray); why blanket spraying fails in the long run.
[Evaluate/Create] NEB answer frame: define with classes → target vs non-target effects → health + environment with biomagnification → safe-use and IPM conclusion with a Terai paddy example.
confusion: Insecticide kills insects, herbicide kills weeds, fungicide kills fungi — match the suffix to the target.
Biomagnification is concentration rising UP the food chain; bioaccumulation is build-up within one body.
Pest resurgence happens because pesticides also kill predators — more spray can mean more pests later.
IPM reduces but does not always eliminate chemicals; 'zero spray' is not the NEB definition.

universalFacts: DDT and BHC are persistent organochlorines; malathion degrades faster — persistence decides exam answers.
Biomagnification explains why top predators suffer most even when water levels look low.
IPM is the NEB-expected conclusion for every pesticide long answer.
examples: DDT sprayed on paddy kills stem borers but also honeybees visiting nearby mustard.
Malathion runoff into a Terai pond kills fingerlings within days.
IPM plot: resistant rice variety plus spider conservation with spray only above threshold.

exercises.question: A paddy farmer sprays DDT every week and washes the tank in the canal. State two effects and one safer practice.
steps: DDT persists and increases in animals higher in the food chain, including fish and birds.
Weekly spraying also selects resistant insects and kills bees.
Washing the sprayer in the canal puts the chemical straight into water.
A safer practice is need-based spraying, protection for the worker, and a waiting period before harvest.
exercises.answer: Biomagnification and resistance. Do not wash sprayers into water. Spray only when the pest count requires it.
